justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: R-01 via 'React SPA Frontend' for customers and brokers, R-02 via adjuster interfaces in 'Web Application Container', and R-03 via 'Migration Router Component' and 'Feature Flag Store' enabling incremental, claim-type by claim-type migration.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Requirement R-05 is directly addressed by 'Read Model Cache Component' (Azure Cache for Redis) serving pre-aggregated claim views under 2 s, decoupled from mainframe latency via asynchronous event synchronization using 'Transactional Store Component' change feeds.
justifications.compatibility: System constraints are respected: 'Mainframe Connector Client' integrates via IBM MQ/TCP, 'Batch Window Gatekeeper' enforces batch timing limits, and 'Legacy Protocol Adapter' acts as an anti-corruption layer to minimize costly mainframe interface changes.
justifications.usability: Both Customers/Brokers and Claims Adjusters are explicitly supported with specialized workflows via 'React SPA Frontend' and 'Node.js BFF', though consolidating both external public users and internal claims adjusters into a single frontend container slightly blurs distinct persona needs.
justifications.reliability: R-04 consistency is ensured via 'Azure Service Bus' queues, 'DLQ Management Service', 'Audit & Reconciliation Component', and 'Resilience4j Circuit Breaker' in 'Migration Router Component', preventing data loss and duplicate processing across batch and real-time processing.
justifications.security: Requirement R-07 is satisfied using 'Active Directory / Azure AD' with OIDC/OAuth2 across frontends and APIs. 'Audit & Compliance Interceptor' and 'Audit & Compliance Logger' ensure transaction integrity, end-to-end traceability, and accountability.
justifications.maintainability: R-06 is fully realized: 'Dynamic Routing Store' and 'Feature Flag Store' in 'Configuration' allow one-day rollbacks of migrated claim types to the mainframe. The anti-corruption architecture ensures loose coupling between cloud microservices and legacy components.
justifications.portability: Target hybrid deployment (azure-westeurope and on-prem-mainframe) is well mapped via Azure Container Apps, App Service, and ExpressRoute. However, high dependency on Azure-specific PaaS services (Cosmos DB, App Configuration) slightly limits portability outside Azure.

PERF-01.justification: Pre-aggregated views in Azure Cache for Redis decouple adjuster queries from 5-second mainframe latency. However, handling cache misses for mainframe-resident data without incurring synchronous legacy call penalties is not fully specified.
sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratios for unmigrated or hybrid claim records
Asynchronous read-model projection latency from mainframe feeds
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency of cached adjuster views versus strict real-time accuracy

PERF-02.justification: Submissions are absorbed by scalable Azure Container Apps and queued asynchronously via Azure Service Bus. The Batch Window Gatekeeper throttles dispatching to protect the fixed 23:00-05:00 nightly batch window.
sensitivity_points: Service Bus queue storage capacity during multi-day submission spikes
Batch Window Gatekeeper dispatch rate limits
tradeoffs: Asynchronous submission acceptance versus immediate transactional confirmation on mainframe

AVAIL-01.justification: Claims Core persists submissions to Cosmos DB and queues them in Azure Service Bus. The Batch Window Gatekeeper explicitly suspends dispatching during batch windows and flushes queued transactions once the window concludes.
sensitivity_points: Queue depth and message time-to-live configuration during extended batch processing
Reliable state detection of mainframe batch start and end
tradeoffs: Decoupled availability during maintenance versus delayed mainframe claim visibility

AVAIL-02.justification: Resilience is provided by Dead Letter Queue management and an Audit & Reconciliation Component reconciling records against legacy batch exports. Exact deduplication keys and distributed two-phase rollback mechanics are not fully detailed.
sensitivity_points: Idempotency key enforcement across hybrid transactional boundaries
Timeliness and granularity of legacy batch export reconciliation
tradeoffs: Asynchronous reconciliation complexity versus synchronous cross-system two-phase locking

MOD-01.justification: The API Gateway, Migration Router, and Azure App Configuration feature flags allow traffic routing by claim type and rapid rollback within minutes without code redeployments or intrusive mainframe modifications.
sensitivity_points: Propagation latency of dynamic routing rules and feature flags
Granularity of routing keys per claim type
tradeoffs: Dynamic configuration management overhead versus deployment simplicity

MOD-02.justification: User interfaces interact purely with the BFF and API Gateway. Modern data persistence and core logic already reside in Azure, allowing decommissioning of mainframe adapters without modifying frontend components.
sensitivity_points: Clean separation between legacy adapter contracts and modern core domain models
Completeness of data migration to Cosmos DB
tradeoffs: Maintaining anti-corruption layers during migration versus direct point-to-point integration

SEC-01.justification: The architecture authenticates via Azure AD and validates tokens at the Node.js BFF and API Gateway. However, fine-grained object-level authorization (broker tenancy and ownership policies) is not explicitly modeled.
sensitivity_points: Enforcement point of fine-grained multi-tenant claim ownership checks
Comprehensive security audit logging for unauthorized access attempts
tradeoffs: Centralized authorization policies at gateway versus domain-level enforcement in core services

SEC-02.justification: Centralized Azure AD handles frontend SSO, but token lifetimes, immediate revocation mechanisms, and propagation of access revocation to on-premises mainframe permissions are unaddressed.
sensitivity_points: OAuth2 access token expiration windows and continuous access evaluation
Synchronization between Azure AD and mainframe security facilities
tradeoffs: Short-lived tokens and token introspection overhead versus stateless performance
